questions.q: Which principle makes it possible to calculate the density of a stone?
questions.why: In water, the stone seems lighter: the water pushes it upwards.

questions.q: What is the formula for density?
choices: d = P air ÷ (P air − P water)

questions.q: A stone weighs 2.00 ct in air and 1.45 ct in water. Its density is about…
What precaution should be taken before weighing in water?
choices: The stone must be dry and with no air bubble stuck to it
questions.why: A bubble would distort the push.

questions.q: What is the approximate density of quartz?
The denser the stone, the more…
choices: the push of the water relieves it little compared with its weight

questions.q: Is density alone enough to identify a stone?
choices: Yes, if the stone is cut
No: several species look alike, so measurements must be cross-checked
questions.why: Each species has its density, but some overlap.
